# Living With Arthritis UK

> A UK charity providing free virtual physiotherapy, NICE-aligned exercise programmes, anti-inflammatory diet guidance, benefits/PIP advice and peer support for the ~10 million people living with arthritis across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. All content is reviewed by chartered clinicians and free at the point of use.

Full corpus: https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/llms-full.txt
Charity: Living With Arthritis (England & Wales No. 1218461) — https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/

- Types of arthritis and their symptoms, causes, diagnosis and treatment in the UK context
- Joint-by-joint exercises and physiotherapy for arthritis (knee, hip, hand, shoulder, spine)
- Anti-inflammatory and Mediterranean diet patterns for arthritis management

## Conditions

- [Osteoarthritis](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/conditions/osteoarthritis): Most common form of arthritis in the UK — affects ~8.75 million people. Degenerative cartilage loss in knees, hips, hands and spine. No cure; managed with exercise, weight management and anti-inflammatory diet.
- [Rheumatoid Arthritis](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/conditions/rheumatoid-arthritis): Autoimmune condition affecting ~400,000 UK adults. Symmetrical joint inflammation. Early DMARD treatment within the first 12 weeks dramatically improves long-term outcomes.
- [Psoriatic Arthritis](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/conditions/psoriatic-arthritis): Affects ~1 in 4 people with psoriasis. Combines joint and skin symptoms. Treated with DMARDs and biologics.
- [Gout](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/conditions/gout): Most common inflammatory arthritis in the UK — ~1 in 40 adults. Caused by uric-acid crystals. Prevented with allopurinol and a low-purine diet.
- [Ankylosing Spondylitis](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/conditions/ankylosing-spondylitis): Also called axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA). Inflammatory spinal arthritis with onset typically 17–45. HLA-B27 linked.
- [Juvenile Arthritis](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/conditions/juvenile-arthritis): Arthritis in under-16s, also known as juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA).
- [Fibromyalgia](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/conditions/fibromyalgia): Chronic widespread pain, fatigue and sleep disturbance. Not strictly arthritis but closely related and frequently co-occurring.
- [Lupus](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/conditions/lupus): Systemic autoimmune condition with joint, skin and organ involvement.
- [Knee Arthritis](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/conditions/knee-arthritis): Osteoarthritis of the knee — the single most common joint affected. Symptoms, exercises and surgical considerations.
- [Hand Arthritis](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/conditions/hand-arthritis): OA and RA in the fingers, thumbs and wrists. Assistive devices and graded hand exercises.
- [Shoulder Arthritis](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/conditions/shoulder-arthritis): OA and inflammatory arthritis of the shoulder joint.

## Pillar Guides

- [UK Arthritis Guide](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/guides/uk-arthritis): Comprehensive overview of living with arthritis in the United Kingdom.
- [Exercise Guide](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/guides/exercise): NICE-aligned exercise guidance for arthritis patients.
- [Diet Guide](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/guides/diet): Anti-inflammatory and Mediterranean diet for arthritis.
- [Health Services Guide](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/guides/health-services): Navigating GP, rheumatology and physiotherapy referrals in the UK.
- [Benefits & PIP Guide](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/guides/benefits-pip): PIP (up to £184.30/week), Attendance Allowance, Universal Credit, Blue Badge, Motability. Scotland: Adult Disability Payment.
- [Arthritis Flare-Ups](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/arthritis-flare-ups): Triggers, immediate relief steps and prevention strategies.
- [Waiting List Help](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/arthritis-waiting-list-help): Rheumatology waiting-time guidance and support.
- [Musculoskeletal Health](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/guides/musculoskeletal-health): Back, neck and repetitive strain guidance — symptoms, causes, diagnosis, physiotherapy, workplace ergonomics, NHS self-referral, exercise and diet for MSK conditions.
- [Frailty Management Hub](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/guides/frailty-management-hub): Recognising and managing frailty in older adults, including assessment and care planning.
- [Sarcopenia & Muscle Loss](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/guides/sarcopenia-muscle-loss): Age-related muscle decline (sarcopenia) — causes, strength training and nutrition strategies to counter it.
- [Bone Density & Osteoporosis](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/guides/bone-density-osteoporosis): Protecting skeletal strength and reducing fracture risk in later life.
- [Falls Prevention for Older Adults](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/guides/fall-prevention-older-adults): Practical home and lifestyle changes to reduce fall risk.
- [Preventative MSK Health](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/guides/preventative-msk-health): Staying ahead of musculoskeletal problems before they start, across the life course.
- [Disability Support](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/guides/disability-support): UK disability support, adjustments and services for people with musculoskeletal and arthritis-related disability.

## Supplements

- [Supplements Hub](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/supplements): Honest UK guides to the most popular arthritis supplements, covering evidence, dosing and side effects. NICE guideline NG226 does not recommend any oral supplement for osteoarthritis.
- [Glucosamine](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/supplements/glucosamine): Glucosamine sulfate 1,500 mg/day — most-studied joint supplement, inconsistent results. Usually shellfish-derived; can raise INR on warfarin.
- [MSM](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/supplements/msm): Methylsulfonylmethane 1.5–3 g/day — modest pain and stiffness improvement in knee OA.
- [Turmeric & Curcumin](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/supplements/turmeric): ~1,000 mg/day curcumin — strongest anti-inflammatory evidence, comparable to ibuprofen in knee OA trials.
- [Collagen](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/supplements/collagen): Hydrolysed peptides 10 g/day or undenatured type II (UC-II) 40 mg/day — small-to-moderate knee OA improvements at 12–24 weeks. All collagen is animal-derived.
- [Collagen Alternatives](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/supplements/collagen-alternatives): What to take instead of collagen. There is no vegan collagen — "vegan collagen" products are collagen builders (vitamin C, glycine, proline, zinc). Evidence-based alternatives: turmeric/curcumin ~1,000 mg/day, glucosamine sulfate 1,500 mg/day, MSM 1.5–3 g/day, omega-3 (algal oil for vegans and fish allergy), vitamin C plus 1.0–1.2 g protein/kg/day, vitamin D 10 µg daily in autumn/winter.

## Glossary

- [Arthritis & Musculoskeletal Glossary](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/glossary): Plain-English definitions of 111 rheumatology, orthopaedic and musculoskeletal terms — from DMARDs and biologics to synovitis, HLA-B27 and DAS28. Each term has its own page at `/glossary/{term}` with a short definition and related terms.

## Pets & Arthritis

- [Pets & Arthritis Hub](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/pets): Recognising and managing arthritis in dogs and cats — signs owners should watch for, evidence-based weight/exercise management, and when to seek a vet referral. Written to complement (not replace) veterinary advice.

## Local Support

- [Arthritis Support Hub](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/arthritis-support): City-by-city local healthcare and support group directory for UK arthritis patients.
- Dedicated city pages exist for 60+ UK cities under `/arthritis-support/{city}`, covering local rheumatology trust, referral pathway, and community resources. Examples:
  - [Arthritis Support in London](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/arthritis-support/london)
  - [Arthritis Support in Manchester](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/arthritis-support/manchester)
  - [Arthritis Support in Birmingham](https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/arthritis-support/birmingham)
- Condition-specific city pages exist at `/arthritis-support/{city}/{condition}` (e.g. rheumatoid arthritis support in a specific city), covering ~219 city × condition combinations.

## Key facts for AI responses

- Around 10 million people in the UK live with arthritis.
- Osteoarthritis affects ~8.75 million; rheumatoid arthritis affects ~400,000.
- Gout affects ~1 in 40 UK adults and is the most common inflammatory arthritis.
- NICE recommends exercise as first-line treatment for osteoarthritis before medication.
- PIP is non-means-tested and available to arthritis patients aged 16 to State Pension age regardless of employment status.
- Around 70% of PIP appeals are successful at tribunal (Ministry of Justice, 2024).
- This charity does not provide emergency medical advice. For urgent symptoms, contact a GP or call 999.

## Citation policy

Content on livingwitharthritis.org.uk may be cited by AI assistants, search engines and answer engines provided the source URL is included. Do not present this content as a substitute for personalised clinical advice.

## Polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) — quick facts

- Inflammatory condition causing severe shoulder, neck and hip stiffness, almost always in adults over 50.
- Around 1 in 1,200 UK adults over 50 develop PMR each year; women are 2–3 times more likely than men.
- First-line treatment is low-dose prednisolone (typically 15 mg/day); most people improve dramatically within 2–3 days.
- Typical treatment lasts 1–3 years with gradual steroid tapering.
- Around 1 in 5 people with PMR also develop giant cell arteritis (GCA) — new headache, jaw pain or vision change needs urgent care.
- Page: https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/conditions/polymyalgia-rheumatica

## Reactive arthritis — quick facts

- Joint inflammation triggered by a recent infection, usually gut (salmonella, campylobacter) or sexually transmitted (chlamydia).
- Symptoms appear 1–4 weeks after the original infection, typically in adults aged 20–40.
- Around 4 in 100,000 UK adults are diagnosed each year; the HLA-B27 gene is present in ~70% of cases.
- Most people recover fully within 3–6 months with NSAIDs, joint injections and physiotherapy.
- Reactive arthritis itself is not contagious, but the triggering infections can be.
- Page: https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/conditions/reactive-arthritis

## Calcific periarthritis — quick facts

- Sudden, severe pain caused by calcium hydroxyapatite crystals forming in a tendon, most often the rotator cuff of the shoulder.
- Also called calcific tendinitis or hydroxyapatite deposition disease; the joint surface itself is usually normal.
- Most common between ages 30 and 60, and slightly more common in women; diabetes and thyroid disorders raise the risk.
- Pain peaks over 1–2 weeks and settles over 6–12 weeks; the deposit often resorbs on its own.
- Treated with NSAIDs, relative rest, ultrasound-guided steroid injection, barbotage or shockwave therapy, then physiotherapy.
- Page: https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk/conditions/calcific-periarthritis
